system_prompt_style.evidence_quote: Modular extensions define tool-use behavior, parsing, prompt shaping, and interaction policies through typed callbacks.
system_prompt_style.note: Extensions rewrite/annotate inputs before LLM calls; prompts also refined by meta-agent.

env_context_strategy.evidence_quote: CCA binds together coding-specific extensions such as file search, file editing, and CLI tools.

context_compaction.evidence_quote: The system then replaces marked historical messages with this compressed summary while maintaining a rolling window of recent messages in their original form.
context_compaction.note: Figure 3 shows truncation of earlier turns before compression.

tool_call_format.evidence_quote: native tool-use models emit structured tool calls that are routed to extension handlers; (2) other models emit XML-style tags (e.g.,<bash>...</bash>)

edit_primitive.note: <file_edit> tag with find/replace semantics; create type also shown in Sec. 2.1.

tool_schema_source.evidence_quote: Each extension is a typed configuration object that registers ordered callbacks
tool_schema_source.note: Prompts/tool wiring authored (and refined by meta-agent); no schema generator described.

protocol_standardization.evidence_quote: The Confucius SDK implements output parsing, tool invocation, and side-effect management viaextensions

loop_primitives.evidence_quote: a minimal, extensible loop that repeatedly calls the LLM, interprets its outputs, and coordinates tool execution

planning_granularity.evidence_quote: theArchitect agent summarizes earlier turns into a structured plan containing goals, decisions, errors, and open TODOs.

multi_agent_topology.evidence_quote: CCA is thus an orchestrator paired with a particular extension bundle
multi_agent_topology.note: Auxiliary Architect and note-taking agents are separate calls, not delegated workers.

delegation_mechanism.evidence_quote: The same orchestrator is reused across all Confucius SDK agents; CCA is one configuration of this loop with coding-oriented extensions enabled.
delegation_mechanism.note: Architect/note-taking agents invoked by the system, not agent-delegated.

human_in_loop.evidence_quote: the percentage of tasks for which the agent’s proposed patch successfully passes all repository-provided tests without human intervention

long_term_memory.evidence_quote: Persistent notes are stored as Markdown files in a file-system-like tree

state_persistence.evidence_quote: agents that improve over time and can pick up long-running projects where they left off
state_persistence.note: Persistent memory/notes across sessions; no explicit resume path documented.

self_verification.evidence_quote: Execution is bounded by a maximum iteration cap, but termination is typically agent-driven.
self_verification.note: No harness-enforced verification described; meta-agent evaluation is offline development-time.

retry_policy.evidence_quote: We report mean Resolve Rate (Pass@1) across three runs.

rollback.evidence_quote: (iii) execute tools (e.g., shell, file edits) and summarize results into memory or artifacts

termination_condition.evidence_quote: Execution is bounded by a maximum iteration cap, but termination is typically agent-driven. Each iteration parses the LLM output into actions; if no further actions are produced, the run ends.

cost_controls.evidence_quote: When the context length approaches configurable thresholds, the Architect Agent is invoked in a separate call
cost_controls.note: Token cost reported but no budget/caching/routing mechanism described.

execution_isolation.evidence_quote: compatible with containerized evaluation environments such as SWE-rex

network_policy.evidence_quote: following the identical environment configuration and infrastructure used by the SWE-Agent baseline

permission_model.evidence_quote: Callbacks share a run context providing I/O, session state, memory, and artifacts
permission_model.note: No approval/allowlist mechanism described; extensions could act as policies.

tracing.evidence_quote: every interaction session is logged into a structured “trajectory”, including user messages, tool invocations, LLM outputs, and system events

replayability.evidence_quote: Each trial is repeated with different random seeds for trajectory sampling to account for randomness in tool invocation and LLM responses.

eval_hooks.evidence_quote: a meta-agent that automates the construction, evaluation, and refinement of agents through a build-test-improve cycle
